questions.q: How many GlideRecord queries does `reassignStaleP1s` execute, regardless of how many incidents match?
options: It depends on how many fallback groups exist
Exactly one — a single query() call combining all four filter conditions
One per matching incident, since each one must be reassigned separately
Two — one to find candidates and one to count them
questions.explain: One GlideRecord is created and .query() is called once; the while(next()) loop then updates each already-found row directly, with no per-row re-query.

questions.q: Why does this method count reassignments with `reassignedCount++` inside the loop instead of calling `.getRowCount()`?
options: Because getRowCount() always returns zero on the incident table
Because getRowCount() can only be called before query() runs
Because the loop is already running and processing each row, incrementing there avoids a separate, redundant query just to get a count
There is no actual difference between the two approaches
questions.explain: getRowCount() would require running (or re-running) the query separately just to get a number the loop can already produce for free while it works.

questions.q: Why is `GlideAggregate` NOT the right tool for the reassignment part of this scenario, even though it's faster for counting?
options: GlideAggregate cannot filter on the priority field
GlideAggregate can only compute totals like COUNT/SUM — it cannot modify individual records, and this method needs to update each matching incident
GlideAggregate requires a GlideRecord to be queried first anyway
GlideAggregate is deprecated in current ServiceNow versions
questions.explain: GlideAggregate is read-only for aggregates — it has no update()/setValue() equivalent, so any task that must change rows needs a real GlideRecord loop.

questions.q: What does `gr.addNullQuery('assigned_to')` contribute to the combined filter in this method?
options: It has no effect since assigned_to is a reference field
It restricts results to incidents with no assignee — the "unassigned" part of the scenario
It restricts results to incidents assigned to the current user
It removes the assigned_to field from the returned records entirely
questions.explain: addNullQuery('assigned_to') filters for the field being empty, which is exactly how "unassigned" is defined in this scenario.

questions.q: Why would adding `.setLimit(n)` to this method's query be incorrect, based on Lesson 16's guidance?
options: setLimit() is for sampling a subset of results; this method's job is to act on every matching incident, not a sample
setLimit() cannot be combined with addNullQuery()
setLimit() would make the query run twice instead of once
setLimit() is only valid when using GlideAggregate
questions.explain: Lesson 16's point about setLimit() was to use it when only a sample is needed — this scenario needs every stale P1 reassigned, so a limit would skip real work.
